name: What is the best layout for a fourplex on a narrow lot?

mainEntity.name: What fourplex floor plan works best on a narrow Los Angeles lot?
mainEntity.text: What fourplex floor plan works best on a narrow Los Angeles lot?

acceptedAnswer.text: Narrow-lot projects are especially common in older Los Angeles neighborhoods, and the wrong layout can waste valuable square footage. Searchers usually want to know whether side-by-side units, stacked units, or a courtyard arrangement works best. The right answer depends on lot width, required setbacks, parking access, and whether the goal is rental income or resale value. In many cases, a stacked configuration with compact circulation is the most efficient, but the design must still preserve light, privacy, and code-compliant egress. A useful page should explain tradeoffs among layouts, including how each affects construction cost, structural complexity, and unit desirability. Readers need more than a floor-plan gallery; they need a practical way to evaluate which arrangement fits their site.
acceptedAnswer.description: On a narrow lot, the best fourplex layout usually prioritizes stacked circulation, efficient unit cores, minimal hallway waste, and a parking strategy that does not consume too much buildable area. The ideal plan depends on frontage, depth, and access.
